chunks: Those against whom the sentence is justified will say: 'O Lord, these are those we had led astray as we had ourselves gone astray. We clear ourselves before You: They never worshipped us.'

key_terms.حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ: Those against whom the divine decree/sentence of punishment has been justified

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'those against whom the sentence is justified' and what do they say on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological shift of the disbelievers' leaders from arrogance to humility as they confront the consequences of their own agency in misguidance. It clarifies that while they initiated the error, the followers' acceptance was a voluntary act, thereby absolving the leaders of being divine objects of worship. This underscores the principle of individual responsibility within the broader framework of divine decree.
